authority: This catalogue owns component-selection metadata. Component guides own syntax and semantics.json owns authored semantics.

components.title: App bar
jobs: Material Design 3 Expressive app bars: small, medium flexible, large flexible, and search, from the HTML.
useWhen: Page title and screen-level actions.
avoidWhen: Peer destinations need navigation; categories need tabs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Small, medium flexible, large flexible, and search app bars.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native header/nav composition; AppBar owns scroll collapse and search expansion.
limitations: Real modal search close/focus ordering and collapsed-header focus clearance are not mapped.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Choose small, flexible medium/large or search app bars for the title and screen actions. Preserve meaningful headings, named actions and reachable controls through scrolling and collapse.

components.selectionExample: A Home/Search/Profile row belongs in navigation, even if placed at the top. Keep the app bar for the title and screen actions.

gaps.description: Real modal search close/focus ordering and collapsed-header focus clearance are not mapped.
gaps.nextStep: Open and dismiss the actual search dialog; Tab through scroll collapse and enlarged headings.

components.title: Bottom app bar
jobs: This screen's commands at the bottom edge, with an optional FAB — not its destinations.
useWhen: Retain an existing bottom app bar or explicit compatibility need.
avoidWhen: New Expressive bottom actions need docked toolbars; destinations need navigation.

implementation.documentedSupport: Bottom command bar with optional FAB.
implementation.webAdaptation: Tab-reachable commands; no toolbar composite role.
limitations: Retained API; use a docked toolbar for new M3 Expressive work when its behavior fits.
Retained baseline bar has no directly mapped target, Tab-order or content-clearance check.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
sections: Toolbars/Overview and Specs: docked toolbar replaces the baseline bottom app bar
upstreamReview.requirements: The docked toolbar replaces the baseline bottom app bar in Expressive guidance. Retain the older bar only for compatibility or a specific capability need.

materialGuidance.reason: Legacy Material component; Google deprecates it for M3 Expressive in favor of docked toolbars.

gaps.description: Retained baseline bar has no directly mapped target, Tab-order or content-clearance check.
gaps.nextStep: Verify fixed-bar clearance at enlarged text; prefer a docked toolbar for new Expressive designs.

components.title: Navigation bar
jobs: Switch between UI views on compact and medium screens.
useWhen: Persistent peer destinations on compact screens.
avoidWhen: Commands need buttons; local panels need tabs.

adaptive.reason: Use persistent peer navigation at wider widths.
Retain a drawer only for an existing interface or a verified capability missing from the target-version expanded rail.

implementation.documentedSupport: Stacked and horizontal destination layouts.
implementation.webAdaptation: Links navigate; the application marks the current destination.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered prose reviewed; collapsed token tables, image-only measurements, runtime and full parity unverified. See the design priority component review for requirement-level findings.

components.selectionExample: Overview/Activity within an account page should not displace Home/Search/Profile in app navigation. Use tabs for those local panels and preserve the app destinations across widths.

components.title: Navigation rail
jobs: Switch between UI views on mid-sized devices.
useWhen: Collapsed, expanded, or modal peer navigation; the Expressive drawer replacement.
avoidWhen: Compact peers fit a navigation bar; verify nesting support.

adaptive.reason: Compact peer destinations fit the bottom edge.
Use the expanded rail when labels should remain visible.
Retain a drawer only for an existing interface or a verified nested-navigation capability missing from the target-version expanded rail.

implementation.documentedSupport: Collapsed, expanded, and modal rails.
implementation.webAdaptation: The compact expanded rail uses a scrim and dismissal behavior.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered prose reviewed; collapsed token tables, image-only measurements, runtime and full parity unverified. See the design priority component review for requirement-level findings.

browserChecks.name: partial replacement and client navigation preserve shell ownership across repeated mounts
browserChecks.scope: Rail shell ownership; enhanced select interaction; generated Menu registry/resource cleanup; tooltip ownership across route replacement.

components.title: Navigation drawer
jobs: A slide-out menu, or a fixed sidebar on Expanded and wider screens.
useWhen: Retain a drawer or a verified nesting capability missing from expanded rails.
avoidWhen: New navigation fits expanded rails; item details need a side sheet.

adaptive.reason: For retained drawers, use the documented modal variant on compact windows.
For retained drawers, use the documented fixed variant on expanded windows.

implementation.documentedSupport: Sliding and fixed drawers with nested sections.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native details/summary supports nesting.
limitations: Retained baseline navigation component; current Expressive guidance points to expanded navigation rail as its replacement.
Breakpoint modal release is checked; nested details and Escape return focus remain distinct checks.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Current Expressive guidance replaces the drawer with an expanded navigation rail. Retained drawers still need named destinations, independent scrolling and correct modal focus and dismissal.

gaps.description: Breakpoint modal release is checked; nested details and Escape return focus remain distinct checks.
gaps.nextStep: Test nested destinations, long scrolling and Escape with the actual trigger.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining fixed drawer releases modal state at the expanded boundary
browserChecks.scope: Compact open to expanded fixed drawer releases native modality and can reopen after returning compact.

components.title: Panes
jobs: Material 3 canonical layouts, from the HTML.
useWhen: Responsive list-detail or supporting layouts.
avoidWhen: A single collection needs a list, not multiple panes.

adaptive.reason: Stack or collapse panes when their container cannot preserve useful pane widths.

implementation.documentedSupport: List-detail, supporting pane, and equal panes.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS viewport and container queries; the application chooses the active compact pane.
limitations: Viewport rules at 840px override narrow-container collapse; compact supporting layouts hide rather than stack supporting content.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
sections: Canonical examples/List-detail and Supporting pane/Across breakpoints
upstreamReview.requirements: List-detail uses one pane on compact windows, usually one on medium and two on expanded windows. Supporting content stacks below primary content on compact and medium windows, then sits alongside it on expanded windows. Preserve selection and scroll state.

materialGuidance.reason: Canonical layout pattern, not a standalone component.

components.selectionExample: A contact directory with no detail view needs a list. Use list-detail panes when selecting a contact reveals a separate detail region.

gaps.description: Viewport rules at 840px override narrow-container collapse; compact supporting layouts hide rather than stack supporting content.
gaps.nextStep: Use an explicit application layout when both panes must remain visible; test actual container width, reading order, selection and scrolling.

browserChecks.name: complete list-detail example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only compact/detail switching, focus return, read state, breakpoint resizing and themed treatments.

components.title: Footer
jobs: Site navigation and extra information at the end of a page.
useWhen: Site links and legal information at page end.
avoidWhen: Primary app destinations need persistent navigation.

implementation.documentedSupport: Native footer with navigation columns and copyright content.
implementation.webAdaptation: Web page landmark styled with theme roles.
limitations: A document-level contentinfo landmark is checked; section-scoped footers and responsive legal links remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use a document footer landmark where appropriate, name distinct navigation groups and preserve meaningful links, reading order and reflow.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: Home/Search/Profile should not require scrolling to a footer. Use a navigation bar or rail for those destinations.

gaps.description: A document-level contentinfo landmark is checked; section-scoped footers and responsive legal links remain unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Place a document footer outside main and sectioning elements; verify named legal navigation at enlarged text.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Tabs
jobs: Material Design 3 tabs, from the HTML.
useWhen: Switch related content panels within one page.
avoidWhen: App destinations need navigation; values need inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Primary and secondary tabs; stacked and horizontal icon layouts.
implementation.webAdaptation: Links target panels; use the shipped runtime keyboard contract.
limitations: Native links use Tab and aria-current; runtime does not implement composite tab arrow keys.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference inputs-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use primary or secondary tabs for related content, with consistent labels and icons, selected state and reachable overflow. Google describes arrow navigation; native anchor navigation is a distinct web adaptation.

components.selectionExample: Home/Search/Profile are app destinations, so use a navigation bar or rail. Overview/Activity panels within one account page can use tabs; Day/Week/Month as a view setting can use segmented inputs.

gaps.description: Native links use Tab and aria-current; runtime does not implement composite tab arrow keys.
gaps.nextStep: Retain native anchor semantics; test overflow and selected-panel focus before adding tab roles.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining suggestions and section links preserve selection and dismissal
browserChecks.scope: Native section links, retained search query and single-select suggestions, Arrow/Enter/Escape/Tab; no spoken-result assertion.

components.title: Breadcrumbs
jobs: The path to this page, from the HTML.
useWhen: Ancestor path to the current page.
avoidWhen: Peer views need tabs; numbered results need pagination.

implementation.documentedSupport: Breadcrumb links and app-bar composition.
implementation.webAdaptation: Labelled navigation with an ordered list and current-page link.
limitations: Named navigation and current-page markup are checked; CSS separator speech and long-path reflow remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use named hierarchy navigation with real ancestor links and a current-page state. It communicates location, not peer categories.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: Overview/Activity/Billing are peers, not ancestors. Use tabs for their same-page panels, not a breadcrumb trail.

gaps.description: Named navigation and current-page markup are checked; CSS separator speech and long-path reflow remain unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Inspect assistive-technology output for separators and test translated paths without truncating essential context.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Pagination
jobs: A list of pages. The HTML is the component.
useWhen: Move through pages of one result set.
avoidWhen: In-page sections need anchors or scrollspy.

implementation.documentedSupport: Page links, active page, and unavailable previous/next items.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS-only navigation; the application supplies destinations.
limitations: aria-disabled and pointer-events alone cannot disable a link for keyboard users.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Name result-page navigation and previous/next actions. Expose the current page and make unavailable actions genuinely unavailable to keyboard users.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: A long article with Introduction/Methods/Results needs section links, optionally with scrollspy, not numbered result pages.

gaps.description: aria-disabled and pointer-events alone cannot disable a link for keyboard users.
gaps.nextStep: Use a non-link unavailable control, verify actual page destinations and preserve current-page state after updates.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Menu
jobs: Material Design 3 menus, from the HTML.
useWhen: Material Design 3 menus, from the HTML.
avoidWhen: The choices need persistent layout space, blocking interaction, or peer navigation.

implementation.documentedSupport: Vertical menus, nested flyouts, grouping, and standard/vibrant styles.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native menu/li structure; Menu owns opening and keyboard behavior.
limitations: Closing animation focus exclusion, submenu RTL, item targets and typeahead need a rendered check.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference inputs-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Choose the current standard, vibrant or grouped menu for a set of choices. Verify 48dp actionable targets, unclipped placement, first-item focus, arrows, typeahead, Escape and submenu navigation. A menu item should not contain multiple independent controls.

gaps.description: Closing animation focus exclusion, submenu RTL, item targets and typeahead need a rendered check.
gaps.nextStep: Exercise a normal-duration closing popup with immediate Tab and Shift+Tab; measure targets and test nested menus.

browserChecks.name: partial replacement and client navigation preserve shell ownership across repeated mounts
browserChecks.scope: Rail shell ownership; enhanced select interaction; generated Menu registry/resource cleanup; tooltip ownership across route replacement.

browserChecks.name: resource observations detect omitted teardown after a partial replacement
browserChecks.scope: Negative control proves resources remain without destroy; no visual parity assertion.

browserChecks.name: Menu cancels superseded callbacks and teardown work (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Open/close reversal and destruction during opening/closing preserve visibility, focus and completion callback ownership. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run in the same file.

components.title: Scrollspy
jobs: Highlight the table of contents as the page scrolls.
useWhen: Track visible sections in a table of contents.
avoidWhen: Separate views need navigation or tabs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Section tracking and table-of-contents links.
implementation.webAdaptation: Web document navigation helper.
limitations: A scoped TOC current link is checked; shared observer behavior with different offsets and multiple independent TOCs remains unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference web-extensions-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use named in-page navigation, real fragment links, stable heading IDs and current-section state. Account for sticky offsets and reduced-motion preferences.

materialGuidance.reason: Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

components.selectionExample: A settings screen with mutually exclusive panels needs tabs. Scrollspy only tracks sections already present in the scrolling document.

gaps.description: A scoped TOC current link is checked; shared observer behavior with different offsets and multiple independent TOCs remains unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Use getActiveElement to select the correct TOC; test independent offsets and teardown before claiming multi-TOC support.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Buttons
jobs: Material Design 3 common buttons, icon buttons, and FABs — from the HTML.
useWhen: Run an action with a visible label.
avoidWhen: Stored choices need inputs; destinations need links.

implementation.documentedSupport: Filled, tonal, outlined, elevated, and text; xsmall through xlarge.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native buttons run commands; a.button links navigate.
limitations: Standalone common buttons do not document a square/toggle shape-morph contract; do not borrow icon-button or connected-group modifiers.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered prose reviewed; collapsed token tables, image-only measurements, runtime and full parity unverified. See the design priority component review for requirement-level findings.

components.selectionExample: A saved delivery-speed choice needs radios or segmented inputs, not three action buttons.

gaps.description: Standalone common buttons do not document a square/toggle shape-morph contract; do not borrow icon-button or connected-group modifiers.
gaps.nextStep: Define and test a standalone shape-morph contract without borrowing connected-group or icon-button modifiers.

browserChecks.name: complete settings example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only responsive layout, targets, keyboard settings and save behavior, themed treatments; no component-wide parity.

browserChecks.name: complete editor example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only input, group toggle, preview/focus, save and bfcache-style remount behavior, themed treatments.

browserChecks.name: complete list-detail example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only compact/detail switching, focus return, read state, breakpoint resizing and themed treatments.

components.title: Icon buttons
jobs: A single icon as the whole control, in four styles and five sizes.
useWhen: Compact actions with recognizable icons.
avoidWhen: An unfamiliar action needs a visible button label.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard, filled, tonal, outlined; five sizes; narrow, wide, and square.
implementation.webAdaptation: Accessible name belongs to the control; the glyph is decorative.
limitations: Elevated and text are not icon-button variants.
Existing group checks cover selected icon colors and press shapes, not all standalone target sizes and disabled states.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Distinguish default and toggle controls, sizes, shapes and widths. Name each action and expose toggle state. Verify 48dp effective targets even for visually smaller sizes, and sufficient icon contrast.

components.selectionExample: A novel approval workflow should use a labeled button. A tooltip on an ambiguous icon cannot replace a clear label or the control's accessible name.

gaps.description: Existing group checks cover selected icon colors and press shapes, not all standalone target sizes and disabled states.
gaps.nextStep: Measure XS/S effective targets and test named default/toggle controls outside groups.

browserChecks.name: button-group toggle colors resolve in a browser
browserChecks.scope: Filled icon button selected color and glyph fill inside a button group only.

browserChecks.name: keyboard press changes icon widths and rendered corners
browserChecks.scope: Icon children inside button group only.

components.title: Segmented buttons
jobs: Two to five connected options, one choice or several, with no script behind them.
useWhen: Choose 2–5 values using native radio/checkbox inputs.
avoidWhen: Independent commands need a standard button group.

implementation.documentedSupport: Single-select radio and multi-select checkbox groups.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native fieldset/input/label owns selection and form values.
limitations: The selected check icon is authored; the framework does not insert it.
Legacy native radio/checkbox contracts lack a directly mapped rendered group check.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use the retained component for two to five single- or multiple-select choices. Current Expressive guidance recommends connected button groups. Preserve form semantics and effective targets when choosing a replacement.

components.selectionExample: Cut/Copy/Paste are commands, not stored choices. Use a standard button group. A shipping-speed value submitted with a form fits single-select segmented inputs with one shared radio name.

gaps.description: Legacy native radio/checkbox contracts lack a directly mapped rendered group check.
gaps.nextStep: Test single/multiple form values and native keys; preserve semantics when choosing connected button groups.

components.title: Button groups
jobs: Related action or toggle buttons that grow and reshape together, in two variants and five sizes.
useWhen: Cluster commands or aria-pressed toggle buttons.
avoidWhen: Submitted values need segmented or other native inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and connected groups; commands and opt-in selection.
implementation.webAdaptation: Runtime coordinates neighboring widths and selection; CSS handles connected shapes.
limitations: Existing geometry and keyboard checks do not cover every required-selection and overflow configuration.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Choose standard or connected groups and optional, required, single or multiple selection deliberately. Verify press growth, shapes, 48dp targets and reachable unwrapped content. Google describes Tab between buttons, with no focus on the group itself.

components.selectionExample: Economy/Express delivery submitted on Save needs radios or segmented inputs. Standard groups fit Cut/Copy/Paste; connected groups fit toggle states, not one-shot commands. A pressed button does not submit a radio value.

gaps.description: Existing geometry and keyboard checks do not cover every required-selection and overflow configuration.
gaps.nextStep: Exercise empty optional and required selection, disabled neighbors and constrained translated labels.

browserChecks.name: button-group toggle colors resolve in a browser
browserChecks.scope: Rendered group behavior; does not establish standalone common/icon-button parity.

browserChecks.name: button-group geometry resolves for overrides, targets, and RTL
browserChecks.scope: Rendered group behavior; does not establish standalone common/icon-button parity.

browserChecks.name: standard press redistribution keeps its rendered width stable
browserChecks.scope: Rendered group behavior; does not establish standalone common/icon-button parity.

browserChecks.name: keyboard press changes icon widths and rendered corners
browserChecks.scope: Rendered group behavior; does not establish standalone common/icon-button parity.

browserChecks.name: complete editor example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only input, group toggle, preview/focus, save and bfcache-style remount behavior, themed treatments.

components.title: Split button
jobs: A lead action and a trailing half that opens a menu of related ones, in five sizes.
useWhen: Default action plus related menu actions.
avoidWhen: Equal actions need a group; values need inputs.

implementation.documentedSupport: Leading action and trailing menu trigger with matching styles.
implementation.webAdaptation: Reuses Menu; no separate split-button runtime.
limitations: Full leading-action versus trailing-menu activation and Escape return are not directly mapped.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Keep the leading default action distinct from the trailing additional-choices menu. Name both controls, expose the trailing expanded state, return focus after dismissal and verify separate 48dp effective targets.

components.selectionExample: PDF/CSV format selection for a later Export action belongs in a select or segmented inputs. A split button fits Export now plus alternate export commands.

gaps.description: Full leading-action versus trailing-menu activation and Escape return are not directly mapped.
gaps.nextStep: Activate both halves with keyboard and pointer; verify expanded state and separate effective targets.

components.title: Floating action button
jobs: A circular action that can open a menu of related shortcuts.
useWhen: A circular action that can open a menu of related shortcuts.
avoidWhen: The action is not the single highest-priority screen action.

adaptive.reason: Use the extended FAB when the action benefits from a visible label.

implementation.documentedSupport: FAB sizes, extended FABs, and menus of related actions.
implementation.webAdaptation: Floating action behavior uses the documented FAB runtime.
limitations: Hover can reveal actions without runtime expanded state; Escape closing can leave focus on a hidden child.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use one primary, non-destructive action. Current guidance discourages the small FAB. Extended FABs have visible labels; FAB menus contain two to six labelled actions and must not hide focused controls.

gaps.description: Hover can reveal actions without runtime expanded state; Escape closing can leave focus on a hidden child.
gaps.nextStep: Reproduce hover and keyboard paths in a browser, unify expanded-state ownership and restore focus when hiding an active child.

components.title: Cards
jobs: Material Design 3 cards, from the HTML.
useWhen: Distinct items with their own content or actions.
avoidWhen: Dense comparable rows need a list.

implementation.documentedSupport: Elevated, filled, outlined, horizontal, and directly actionable cards.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native article anatomy; primary-action links preserve navigation semantics.
limitations: Existing card lifecycle and geometry evidence does not cover every selected variant, contrast and reflow state.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference feedback-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Group one related subject in an elevated, filled or outlined card. A whole-card primary action must not contain other actions. Avoid unnecessary containment and internal scrolling; provide alternatives to drag and swipe gestures.

components.selectionExample: A hundred compact activity records need a list. Giving every row a card adds separation without a separate content or action group.

gaps.description: Existing card lifecycle and geometry evidence does not cover every selected variant, contrast and reflow state.
gaps.nextStep: Measure and keyboard-test the chosen variant with long content and nested controls.

browserChecks.name: dragged and picked-up states override simultaneous pointer states
browserChecks.scope: Specific card state, disclosure fallback, or horizontal layout contract.

browserChecks.name: invalid disclosures keep their panels visible and operable
browserChecks.scope: Specific card state, disclosure fallback, or horizontal layout contract.

browserChecks.name: directly actionable horizontal cards use intrinsic or fixed heights at the breakpoint
browserChecks.scope: Specific card state, disclosure fallback, or horizontal layout contract.

browserChecks.name: expanding-card completion follows CSS and survives interruption (chromium)
browserChecks.scope: Chromium: zero and 1.2s container timing, reopening, cancellation, native close, removal, destruction and focus return. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run separately in the browser suite.

components.title: Lists
jobs: Continuous vertical indexes of text and images.
useWhen: Scan repeated rows of text and images.
avoidWhen: Rich independent items need cards.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and segmented lists.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native list semantics; visual selection alone does not justify aria-selected.
limitations: Ordinary native lists and child controls do not implement Google composite arrow navigation.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference feedback-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
sections: Accessibility/Indicate selection with more than color, Focus, Platform-specific labels
upstreamReview.requirements: Choose ordinary content, actionable rows or selection explicitly. Use consistent slots and alignment, 48dp targets and a selection cue beyond color. Google describes composite arrow navigation for actionable lists and listbox/option semantics for web selection; these do not apply automatically to ordinary lists.

components.selectionExample: A product with a large image, description, price, and several actions may need a card. A simple product-name index remains a list.

gaps.description: Ordinary native lists and child controls do not implement Google composite arrow navigation.
gaps.nextStep: Retain native semantics unless a complete composite is supplied; test row control names and selection meaning.

browserChecks.name: complete list-detail example preserves both treatments and its task path
browserChecks.scope: Example-only compact/detail switching, focus return, read state, breakpoint resizing and themed treatments.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining web navigation, badges and list controls expose their meaning
browserChecks.scope: Named navigation, document footer, unavailable pagination non-link, named badge count, list checkbox and scoped TOC aria-current. No spoken-output assertion.

components.title: Dialogs
jobs: Important prompts in a user flow. Dedicated to a single task.
useWhen: Focused prompts or decisions that interrupt the flow.
avoidWhen: Ignorable feedback needs snackbar or banner.

implementation.documentedSupport: Basic and full-screen dialogs.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native dialog.showModal()/close(); shared dialog behavior is separate from AutoInit.

upstreamReview.note: Rendered prose reviewed; collapsed token tables, image-only measurements, runtime and full parity unverified. See the design priority component review for requirement-level findings.

components.selectionExample: Saving successfully should not force dismissal of a dialog. Use a snackbar for that feedback and a banner for a persistent nonblocking issue; reserve a confirmation dialog for a decision that must precede the action.

components.title: Bottom sheet
jobs: Secondary content anchored to the bottom of the screen.
useWhen: Secondary content anchored to the bottom of the screen.
avoidWhen: Persistent wider-window secondary content or a small anchored choice fits another component.

adaptive.reason: Persistent secondary content fits beside the main task.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and modal bottom sheets.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native dialog.show()/showModal(); shared runtime handles dragging and dismissal.
limitations: The shared handle dismisses rather than cycling sheet heights; long-content and drag behavior are outside the new modal check.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Distinguish standard and modal sheets. Keep overflowing content scrollable, close actions reachable and height changes available without dragging. Verify the selected width and margin configuration against Google measurements.

gaps.description: The shared handle dismisses rather than cycling sheet heights; long-content and drag behavior are outside the new modal check.
gaps.nextStep: Use explicit close controls; separately verify reachable scrolling and any application-owned height changes.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining sheet variants retain native modal focus and explicit close actions
browserChecks.scope: Each native dialog variant: modal containment, Escape, explicit close/return focus and nonmodal outside focus. No drag or long-content assertion.

components.title: Side sheet
jobs: Optional content and actions, without interrupting the main view.
useWhen: Optional content and actions, without interrupting the main view.
avoidWhen: The content is peer navigation or requires a blocking modal decision.

adaptive.reason: Secondary content must fit a compact window.
Use a dialog when a compact task must block progress.

implementation.documentedSupport: Standard and modal side sheets.
implementation.webAdaptation: Native dialog and shared drag/dismiss behavior.
limitations: Native modal/nonmodal focus is checked; start-docked RTL drag direction and long-content fit remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
upstreamReview.requirements: Use standard or modal sheets for optional supporting content. Mirror the trailing edge in RTL, avoid horizontal scrolling and provide an accessible close action separate from dragging.

gaps.description: Native modal/nonmodal focus is checked; start-docked RTL drag direction and long-content fit remain unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Test the actual RTL edge, drag alternative, enlarged labels and reachable close action.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining sheet variants retain native modal focus and explicit close actions
browserChecks.scope: Each native dialog variant: modal containment, Escape, explicit close/return focus and nonmodal outside focus. No drag or long-content assertion.

components.title: Floating sheet
jobs: Secondary content on a surface that floats free of every window edge.
useWhen: Detached secondary content or tools.
avoidWhen: Urgent decisions need dialogs; edge content needs sheets.

implementation.documentedSupport: Inset floating dialog surface.
implementation.webAdaptation: Shares Dialogs initialization; no edge attachment or drag handle.
limitations: Native dialog focus and close are checked; long-content zoom and inset geometry remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference layout-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference feedback-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
sections: Guidelines/Accessibility requirements for web, Placement, Behavior
Accessibility/Interaction & style, Accessibility requirements on web, Focus, Keyboard navigation
upstreamReview.requirements: Show one snackbar at a time without autofocus or a focus trap. Actionable snackbars persist until acted on or dismissed. Timed web feedback needs an equivalent persistent inline message. Document a keyboard route to actions, support Escape when focused and restore logical focus.

components.selectionExample: A successful save can use a snackbar. Offline status that still allows editing needs a persistent banner; a required irreversible-delete confirmation needs a dialog before the action.

gaps.description: Focus/hover pause does not satisfy persistent actionable snackbar guidance; default action timeout is finite and Escape handling is absent.

materialGuidance.reason: Retained framework pattern absent from the reviewed current M3 component inventory; related current guidance does not certify this implementation.

components.selectionExample: A Saved message should not leave a permanent banner. Use a snackbar. A sync outage that permits local edits fits a banner; an unavoidable decision fits a dialog. This banner is a framework feedback pattern, not a verified current M3 component.

gaps.description: Legacy/related banner styling supplies no announcements, dismissal or focus recovery.
gaps.nextStep: Implement application-owned status updates and named actions; verify text enlargement and focus after removal.

components.title: Progress indicators
jobs: Activity and progress. The HTML is the indicator.
useWhen: Measured progress or longer indeterminate waits.
avoidWhen: Brief unknown waits fit loading indicator; instant work needs none.

implementation.documentedSupport: Linear and circular progress, determinate and indeterminate.
implementation.webAdaptation: Prefer native progress where applicable; supply accessible state for custom hosts.
limitations: Reduced-motion static custom fill is checked; forced colors and native indicator rendering remain unverified.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference feedback-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
sections: Guidelines/Usage, Progress indicators in buttons, Responsive layout
upstreamReview.requirements: Report accurate determinate values and omit values for unknown progress. Keep the same process recognizable when its state changes. Mirror linear progress in RTL and provide an end stop when track contrast needs it. Loading indicators cover many short waits; circular progress remains useful in buttons and processes that become determinate.

components.selectionExample: A two-second refresh with no measured fraction fits a loading indicator. An upload with bytes transferred needs determinate progress, even if short; a long job with no fraction can use indeterminate progress. Never invent a percentage. Indeterminate linear bars remain supported; the short-wait replacement specifically targets indeterminate circular spinners.

gaps.description: Reduced-motion static custom fill is checked; forced colors and native indicator rendering remain unverified.
gaps.nextStep: Test native and custom determinate/indeterminate variants, visible static feedback and changing accessible values.

gaps.description: Custom linear progress uses physical left fill in RTL; end-stop and wavy Expressive variants are not verified.
gaps.nextStep: Test RTL native and custom bars; repair mirrored custom fill and assess an end stop for insufficient track contrast before claiming current variant parity.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining progress and loading variants stop spatial motion
browserChecks.scope: Named progress state, reduced-motion animation removal and visible custom static fill; no spoken-delivery assertion.

components.title: Loading indicator
jobs: A shape that morphs while it spins, for waits under five seconds.
useWhen: Brief waits under about five seconds, no known fraction.
avoidWhen: Measured or long-running work needs progress.

implementation.documentedSupport: Uncontained and contained morphing loading indicator.
implementation.webAdaptation: CSS-only; the author supplies an accessible waiting message.
limitations: The framework requires a named status while Google recommends progressbar; an indeterminate progressbar validly omits aria-valuenow.

upstreamReview.note: Requirements and boundaries: design reference feedback-material-review. Full visual parity and spoken output unverified.
sections: Accessibility/Use cases, Interaction & style, Labeling elements
upstreamReview.requirements: Use for an actual short wait with unknown progress, usually 200ms to five seconds. Do not use for a process that will become determinate. Google specifies a descriptive progressbar role and sufficient shape contrast; a refresh gesture still needs an alternative.

components.selectionExample: A file upload reporting 42% needs determinate progress, not the morphing loading shape. A longer unmeasured job needs indeterminate progress. Do not flash an indicator for an effectively instant response or announce a fabricated value.

gaps.description: The framework requires a named status while Google recommends progressbar; an indeterminate progressbar validly omits aria-valuenow.
gaps.nextStep: Record this current contract difference; test meaningful waiting text and spoken delivery. Choose a progress indicator initially when a transition to determinate progress is expected.

browserChecks.name: chromium: remaining progress and loading variants stop spatial motion
browserChecks.scope: Named progress state, reduced-motion animation removal and visible custom static fill; no spoken-delivery assertion.

materialMappingPolicy.implementation: documentedSupport is a source-reviewed summary for frameworkVersion, not a complete variant inventory or a browser pass; guideSource identifies the owning contract section.
materialMappingPolicy.upstream: relationship identifies an upstream component (including explicitly marked legacy components), layout pattern, related guidance, or framework extension. upstreamReview states exactly which source and scope were reviewed; a link alone is not a specification review.
materialMappingPolicy.parity: Full upstream parity and browser conformance are not assessed by this mapping. Unlisted limitations are unknown, not evidence of completeness.

implementation.documentedSupport: Fifteen baseline type-role utilities and rem-based tokens; semantic element defaults; separate brand/plain/fallback font tokens; bundled Latin Roboto and Noto Sans 400/500. Existing role-weight tokens permit scoped application emphasis.
implementation.webAdaptation: Use supported web component and application overrides; Android attributes and APIs are design references only.

gaps.description: No emphasized role utilities or emphasized token family; emphasized labels and smaller titles requiring 700 need an application-supplied real face.
gaps.nextStep: Define an additive emphasized-scale contract and a font-loading policy before implementing public names.

gaps.description: Bundled text fonts cover Latin and 400/500 only; a Noto Sans fallback declaration does not establish non-Latin coverage.
gaps.nextStep: Add browser checks for actual rendered font faces/weights, representative scripts, and all type-role metrics; retain native zoom/assistive review separately.

gaps.description: No shared md-sys-shape token family or general rounded/cut-corner theming system.

implementation.documentedSupport: Component-owned CSS/runtime motion, sampled fast-spatial linear easing for button-group width/radius, expanding-card container transition, and scale utility. Button groups, expanding cards and the scale utility suppress transitions under reduced motion. Expanding-card close cleanup follows the actual container transition, including CSS timing overrides and cancellation.
implementation.webAdaptation: Use supported web component and application overrides; Android attributes and APIs are design references only.

gaps.description: No shared md-sys-motion token family, general spring solver, or unified motion-theme selector.
gaps.nextStep: Define shared semantic timing/spring roles only after mapping existing component needs; distinguish spatial and effects motion without presenting sampled CSS easing as a general solver.

browserChecks.scope: Chromium: reduced-motion final transforms, active transition cancellation, focus preservation and card close cleanup. Equivalent Firefox and WebKit cases run separately in the browser suite.
